patterns: Character reveal beats everything: azed_ai's '2D to 3D, meet my latest character creation' hit 118.5K views, 1,717 likes and 245 bookmarks - a single transformation clip with a one-line hook.

The 'X but it's 197x' format bounced back when tied to the news: techhalla's 'Claude is down but it's 1981' (17.8K, made in Magnific, recipe in reply) and 'Zelda: Breath of the Wild but it's 1973' (16.9K). maxescu's World of Warcraft 1975/1981 versions stayed under 2.1K, so the IP pick and timing matter more than the format.

Launch-day news recaps carry reach: minchoi's 'Google just dropped Gemini 4 Hydrogen, 10 wild examples' did 85.8K, plus Antigravity Orchestrator (9.8K) and ChatGPT Dot (7.9K). The Claude outage itself made Salmaaboukarr's 3-word 'claude is down?!' a 16.0K post.

Outside the watchlist, model face-offs dominate: Fable 5.2 vs Gemini 4 Carbon/Hydrogen cost-and-quality tests (luckeyfaraday 27.0K, AIMind_Ai 20.2K, noclipepe 9.2K), and MiniMax H3 Image ranked #1 open-weights image model (ArtificialAnlys 21.9K). A wave of #ad posts for Sume Director Studio 1.0 also ran (HanaOnAi 21.0K, MiraSynth0 18.2K).

Process posts still earn saves: shedntcare_'s 'keyframes, character consistency, outfits first' (41.6K, last 48h) and AIWarper's fully synthetic Iron Maiden-style video experiment (8.0K, 79 bookmarks).

drafts.draft_en:
2D to 3D.

One concept sketch → one VFX-ready character.

Same workflow I used on House of David S2. Breakdown below 👇
drafts.video_tip: 8-12s: hold the flat 2D sketch for 1s, then a smooth turntable reveal of the 3D character with lighting; end on a hero pose. No text overlay beyond '2D → 3D'. Prompts + steps in the first reply.

drafts.draft_en:
Saturday Challenge 🎞️

This week: take ONE 2D character and bring it into 3D.

Sketch, turnaround, final shot. Post yours below 👇 I'll feature my top 3 next Saturday.
drafts.video_tip: 6-8s teaser: your own sketch morphs into a 3D turntable, then a 'SATURDAY CHALLENGE' title card. Pin it for the weekend.

drafts.draft_en:
House of David, but it's 1973 🎞️

Same epic. Grainy film stock, practical-looking VFX, 70s zooms.

Would you watch this cut?
drafts.video_tip: 12-15s: 4-5 shots with 70s film grain, warm halation, crash zooms and a mono title card. Keep the first shot instantly recognizable. Put the recipe (model + grade settings) in the reply, like techhalla did.

drafts.draft_en:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen vs Fable 5.2 vs my VFX pipeline.

Same shot brief. Which one would you put on screen? 1, 2 or 3 👇
drafts.video_tip: Split screen in 3 panels with labels 1/2/3 only (no model names on screen) for 6-8s, then the reveal in the reply. Use the exact same plate and timing in each panel.

drafts.draft_en:
Keyframes first. Characters locked. Costumes locked.

Only then do I animate.

That's the whole secret of consistent AI VFX characters.
drafts.video_tip: 10-15s: a grid of 4 locked keyframes for 2s, then each tile animates in sequence into the final shot. Prompts in the reply.
